results.title: Who sold the most books in 2025? | The Horror Tree
results.content:
Who sold the most books in 2025?

Who sold the most books in 2025?
Who sold the most books in 2025?
I have been looking back at who sold the most books each year since 2022 here at Horror Tree. Every year, this question is not as easy to answer as it seems as each site has different information and metrics, but often, the same names and books pop up on most of the lists. I work to balance variety with accuracy when I choose the authors to feature, that is why once again, this list will be ten of the best-selling authors in 2025 (in no particular order) based on a variety of sources listed at the end of the article. If you are interested in who was on top the last three years, you can find them here: 2022, 2023, 2024.
To the surprise of no one, the Top Five Publishers dominate the best-seller lists each year, with Penguin Random House at the top with 38% of hardcover bestsellers in 2025. Indie and small presses make up a much smaller share of the market, but hardcover sales for the Top Five slipped down to 83% of the market from 86% in 2024, showing a modest growth for independent publishers. As well, the Independent Publisher Caucus, a collective of 117 small and independent publishers, launched the Independent Press Top 40 bestseller list in tandem with the American Booksellers Association this year with weekly bestseller lists of books from indie presses being sold at indie bookstores across the USA. I am excited about this because it will make it easier for me to include more indie best-sellers on this list next year.
Top-Selling Books: Sunrise on the Reaping, The Hunger Games
Suzanne Collins is one of the most famous authors of children’s and young adult fiction. She is best known for her dystopian YA series, The Hunger Games, and her children’s fantasy series, The Underland Chronicles. Collins began her career in 1991 as a writer for children’s television shows. She made the transition to books when she came up with the idea for The Underland Chronicles and wrote five books between 2003 and 2007. Then, in 2008, she published the first book in The Hunger Games trilogy, followed by a prequel in 2020.
2025 saw the release of a second Hunger Games prequel, Sunrise on the Reaping (SotR), which focuses on the backstory of Katniss’ mentor, Haymitch Abernathy and his time in the games. SotR catapulted to the top of the children and YA bestseller list, selling over 2 million hardcovers (including the one on my own shelf). As well, a feature film based on the book is coming to theatres this November. The success of SotR also boosted Collins’ other works, with The Hunger Games reappearing on top selling lists.
Top-Selling Books: The Housemaid, The Housemaid’s Secret, The Tenant, The Crash
For the third year in a row now, Freida McFadden has found her way onto this list with her psychological thrillers. McFadden is the pseudonym of Sarah Cohen. Cohen’s first career was as a physician. She studied mathematics at Harvard University and later attended medical school. Throughout her career in medicine, she was writing fiction and submitting manuscripts. She self-published her first book in 2013, and since then, she has published 30 novels, including The Housemaid, which was adapted into a film in 2025 starring Amanda Seyfried and Sydney Sweeney. Beyond this, she had eight books that held double-digit stays on the bestseller list in 2025.
Top-Selling Books: Fourth Wing, Iron Flame, Onyx Storm
None of my best-selling lists would be complete without at least one Romantasy bestseller. This year, it is Rebecca Yarros who dominated the book lists. Her best-known series is the Empyrean series. The first book, Fourth Wing was released in April 2023, followed by Iron Flame in November. The third book in the series, Onyx Storm, came out in January 2025 and sold more than 2.7 million copies within the first week. As well, in January, she held the top 3 spots on the New York Times’ hardcover bestseller list.
Yarros began writing while her husband was deployed in Afghanistan. Fourth Wing is her 20th novel. Along with her sons, Yarros has Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, which is a genetic connective tissue disorder. She cites her illness as one of her inspirations, as she had never read a fantasy novel that had a protagonist with physical limitations like hers, so she chose to write one.
Top-selling book: The Let Them Theory
Each year, I like to include at least one top-selling non-fiction book, and this year, Mel Robbins’ book, The Let Them Theory (TLTT) was an easy choice since it was the #1 best selling book on Amazon in 2025. Originally published in 2024, TLTT climbed the list in 2025 in part because Robbins went on her first global speaking tour, which began on May 2, 2025 and visited 31 cities across North America. The book is a self-help book that focuses on letting go of other people’s judgments and opinions. Robbins also hosts a podcast and has written two other self-help books.
Top-selling book: The Black Wolf
Louise Penny is a Canadian author of crime fiction. Her most famous series stars Chief Inspector Armand Gamache and is set in Quebec. She has sold millions of copies worldwide and has repeatedly been featured in the number 1 spot on the New York Times Best Seller List. Her latest book in the series, The Black Wolf, in which Gamache has to stop a deadly terrorist ring, reached the number one spot in November 2025. As well, The Black Wolf was the bestselling book by a Canadian author in Canada for 2025.
Percival Everett is an American Pulitzer Prize-winning author and a professor of English who has written over 20 novels as well as numerous short stories and poetry. In 2024, he published James, a reimagining of the Adventures of Huckleberry Finn by Mark Twain, told from the point of view of the slave, Jim, who travels with him. James won both a National Book Award and the Pulitzer Prize. In 2025, Everett was the bestselling Black author in 2025, according to a new list compiled by the African American Literature Book Club, beating out Kamala Harris and Octavia E. Butler.
Top-selling book: The Secret of Secrets
Dan Brown wrote a few books before hitting the best seller list with his breakout hit, The Da Vinci Code in 2003. Due to its success, his previous books, which had seen little success, reached the bestseller list in 2004. The protagonist of his series is Robert Langdon, a Harvard University professor who goes on thrilling treasure hunts, reminiscent of Indiana Jones. The Secret of Secrets is the sixth book in this series and was at the number one spot on the New York Times Bestseller List for two weeks in a row in 2025.
Top-selling book: Partypooper (Diary of a Wimpy Kid #20)
Of the top twenty bestselling books of 2025, according to Publishers Weekly, seven are children’s books, the top of which belongs to Jeff Kinney, author of the Diary of a Wimpy Kid series. The series is an illustrated children’s novel series and media franchise that follows a middle-schooler named Greg Heffley who illustrates his life in the eponymous diary. Kinney first came up with the characters in 1998, but spent eight years conceiving the first book before showing it to a publisher. The series began as a website with daily entries before Kinney signed a multi-book deal in 2006 to launch the book series. It has been a remarkable hit, and this is the third time I have included him on this list.
Top-selling books: Big Jim Begins (Dog Man #13), Big Jim Believes (Dog Man #14)
With two of the seven spots on the top 20 list, Dav Pilkey certainly deserves to be included on this list for the third time, as well. Pilkey’s Dog Man series is about a crime-fighting dog who likes to dress up as “The Bark Knight”. The series is a spin-off of Pilkey’s other famous series, Captain Underpants. The titular Big Jim is a cat who is a friend of Dog Man, and has his own superhero identity, “Commander Cupcake”. Pilkey wrote his first book in 1987, World War Won, and published Captain Underpants in 1997.
Top-selling book: Lights Out
My last entry, Lights Out by Navessa Allen, is very different from the last two books. Described as a “fast-paced dark romance with a morally gray male lead,” this book comes with a long list of trigger warnings. I am including it because it is the bestselling book from an independent publisher (Zando), having sold more than 595,000 copies and sitting at number eleven on Publisher Weekly’s top 20 list. Allen has had a variety of jobs, bartending, serving in the military, building flight simulators, farming, etc. She worked these jobs while pursuing her career as a full-time writer.

Melody lives in Ontario, Canada and writes short, speculative fiction that has been published by several small presses. She is also an avid reviewer who writes reviews and articles for The Horror Tree and on her blog, Melody Writes. Melody is a member of Sisters in Crime and is the secretary for the Ontario chapter of the Horror Writers Association. She earned her Master of Arts studying Ancient Greek and Roman Studies and often infuses her work with elements of Greek mythology.

results.content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
This is a list of lists of bestselling novels in the United States as determined by Publishers Weekly. The list features the most popular novels of each year from 1895 through 2020.
The standards set for inclusion in the lists – which, for example, led to the exclusion of the novels in the Harry Potter series from the lists for the 1990s and 2000s – are currently unknown.
For many years, the list was maintained by Alice Payne Hackett, who also published a decennial series which summarized and commented on the best sellers of the previous decade. Her Seventy Years of Bestsellers 1895–1965 was published in 1970.
